newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress to work through July recess.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress to work through July recess.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso will call an extraordinary session of Congress to run through the month of July, which is normally a recess, a government official in Congress said Wednesday.
"It's been decided. There will be an extraordinary session," said an aide to Deputy Luis Eduardo Magalhaes, the government's chief whip in the Chamber of Deputies.
The announcement had been expected after months of delay in voting on key pieces of legislation in Congress.
The Chamber of Deputies has been trying to vote on amendments to a crucial civil service reform bill since April and a pension reform bill is awaiting a vote in a Senate committee.

Other important issues which may be dealt with in July include extension of a Fiscal Stabilization Fund, a key tool in the government's battle to control public spending, and bills in the Senate regulating the telecommunications and oil industries.
While the extraordinary session is a blow to congressional officials and journalists who had looked forward to a quiet month in Brasilia, lawmakers were likely to be in favor of the idea.
They are entitled to triple pay during extraordinary sessions, taking their salary for July to a cool $23,000 each.
